name: What happens to pool equipment after the pool is removed?

mainEntity.name: Are pumps, filters, heaters, and plumbing lines removed, capped, or left in place?
mainEntity.text: Are pumps, filters, heaters, and plumbing lines removed, capped, or left in place?

acceptedAnswer.text: Pool equipment should not be an afterthought in a removal project. Pumps, filters, heaters, electrical lines, and exposed plumbing can all affect the final cost and safety of the site. In many jobs, the equipment pad is removed or disconnected, and old components are hauled off as part of the demolition. Plumbing lines may be capped or abandoned depending on how the yard will be reused and what the permit scope allows. Homeowners should ask whether the bid includes removal of the equipment pad, conduit, gas lines, and visible plumbing. If the plan is to install a new patio, garden, or structure later, leaving old lines in place can create future obstacles. A good estimate should state what happens to every visible component, not just the shell itself. That prevents disputes after the pool is gone.
acceptedAnswer.description: Pool equipment is usually removed or disconnected during demolition, but the exact scope should be specified in the contract. Pumps, filters, heaters, and exposed plumbing may be hauled away, capped, or abandoned depending on the project plan and local requirements.
